title: Priority-windowed KV-staging and slimline batcher for heterogeneous prompt/response workloads
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts, long generator responses, and long context retrievals) are causing inefficient continuous-batcher packing and high KV cache fragmentation across GPU slabs. We observe frequent per-request slab splits and late-stage preemption that increases 95th latency and token cost. Goal: Implement a lightweight 'slimline batcher' that uses a small in-memory KV staging layer and priority-windowed scheduling to improve packing for short/medium requests while preventing long response tails from blocking slots and fragmenting GPU slabs. Approach: 1) Add a per-worker KV-staging buffer (staging lanes) that holds hot KV entries for short-lived dialogs instead of immediately pinning into GPU slabs. 2) Introduce priority-window bins: incoming requests are classified into short/medium/long windows based on observed token budget and recent sequence length histograms; the scheduler maintains separate coalesce windows so long tails are batched separately and don't dilute short-request batching. 3) Slimline batcher: a low-overhead coalescer that favors compact slot packing for short requests and defers slab pinning until a request reaches a configurable warmup threshold or when KV hits cross a threshold. 4) KV residency hints: requests carry a residency_hint header which biases the staging buffer to promote entries to GPU-only KV when they exceed a TTL or read-count. 5) Eviction coordination: a background compaction job merges small fragments into contiguous slabs during low-utilization periods. Expected outcomes: fewer slab splits, less GPU fragmentation, improved throughput for short requests, and lower p95/p99 latency for mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency for mixed workload decreases by >= 12% on benchmark suite
GPU memory fragmentation index (internal metric) reduces by >= 20% across sustained 2-hour load tests
No regression in throughput for long-response-only workload (<= 3% throughput drop)
End-to-end correctness: no KV misses/incorrect responses introduced by staging under A/B run
Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 feature flag and disabled by default for Private customers until opt-in
comments: 2026-03-02 - Riley Chen: Spiked prototype of per-worker KV staging in rust-runtime branch 'kv-staging-spike'. Observed reduced immediate slab allocations but saw a corner where repeated short re-promotions caused thrashing. Added an LRU decay to staging lanes.

2026-03-04 - Diego Martinez: Implemented priority-window classifier based on empirical 95th percentiles from trace-2026-02 (short < 32 tokens, medium 32-512, long > 512). Tuned window timers to 12ms/50ms/200ms respectively in local sim.

2026-03-06 - Diego Martinez: First integrated slimline coalescer. In the sim harness (1000 TPS mixed), p95 improved 9% but GPU fragmentation unchanged. Hypothesis: promotion heuristics are too eager; will add a 'read-count' gate before promoting to slab.

2026-03-08 - Asha Patel (perf): Ran 2-hour soak on aws-g4dn cluster. Observed slab split events down 27% and staging memory steady at ~750MB/worker. Measured p95 down 15% and token throughput +4% for mixed workload. Attaching dashboard.

2026-03-10 - Product review (Eliot Brooks): Flags and console controls requested: max staging size per-worker, residency_hint override, and rollout knob for canary. Also requested safe-fallback to existing KV behavior on OOM.
2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez: Code PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1947. Includes unit tests for LRU decay, promotion threshold, and compaction trigger. QA scheduled for 2026-03-15.

2026-03-12 - Riley Chen: Noted edge-case where long sequence replay after promotion caused eviction storms across GPUs in multi-tenant Dedicated. Mitigation: add tenant-aware promotion caps and slow-path backpressure to avoid cross-tenant eviction amplification. Created follow-up task ENG-998002 to finalize tenant caps.
notes: Implementation constraints: keep added memory per-worker < 1GB to avoid squeezing smaller Dedicated shapes. Prefer lock-free ring buffers for staging lanes. Use existing telemetry points for promotion/read-count to avoid heavy new metrics. Rollout plan: feature flag -> internal canary (10% requests) -> internal prod (50%) -> opt-in customers -> global enable. Monitoring: slab-split-rate, staging-residency, promotion-rate, p95/p99 latency by window. If p99 regresses by >10% during canary, auto-rollout rollback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Staging promotes too late causing cache miss penalty -> Mitigation: conservative promotion gate + adaptive promotion if miss-rate climbs
Risk: Thundering promotion from staging to slab causing eviction storms -> Mitigation: rate-limit promotions per-worker and tenant, add jitter to background compaction
Risk: Increased memory footprint for Private deployments -> Mitigation: feature off-by-default in private, exposed config for max_staging_bytes per-instance
